notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. The only source is the tnlandforms list (coordinates and an elevation of 362 with no unit labelled); the list gives no register cross-reference, and the record has none either. The record's elevation_m of 110.3 matches 362 ft, so the story reads the figure as feet and says so. Searches found no fire tower history for St. Clair or Burke County. A Watch Duty entry for a January 2026 fire on St. Clair Road in Keysville is unrelated and not used. A towerdex snippet about a roughly 315 ft Keysville structure looks like a communications tower and is not used. The story is about 100 words, under the 120-word guide floor, on purpose. The NHLR and FFLOS counts come from the local crawl copy; its full NHLR list has no St. Clair. Fact-check 2026-10-21: flagged the unlabelled elevation unit in the story, added the missing footnote to the first sentence, and narrowed 'No source describes' to the sources read. The Tom Dunigan credit is not on the Georgia page; it comes from the same site's Tennessee page footer.
